record.original_question: For the unit sphere S^{n-1}, what is the smallest number of pairwise disjoint balls whose centers lie on S^{n-1} and which guarantee that every straight line passing through the center of the sphere intersects at least one of those balls?

evidence.quote: Problem 7. (The shadow problem). What is minimal number of pair wise disjoint balls with the centre on sphere Sn−1 it is enough that any straight line, getting through the centre of the sphere, crossed at least one of those balls?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^{n-1} = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^n : \|x\| = 1\}$ denote the unit sphere in $\mathbb{R}^n$ (with $n \ge 2$), and let $O$ be its center (the origin). A "ball" means a closed Euclidean ball $B(c,r) \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ of some radius $r > 0$ whose center $c$ lies on $S^{n-1}$. A finite collection $B_1,\dots,B_N$ of such balls is called pairwise disjoint if $B_i \cap B_j = \emptyset$ for all $i \ne j$ (the radii of the balls are not prescribed and may differ from ball to ball, but none of them contains $O$). The collection is said to "cast a full shadow at $O$" if every straight line in $\mathbb{R}^n$ passing through $O$ intersects at least one of the balls $B_i$.

Determine the minimal number $N(n)$ of pairwise disjoint balls with centers on $S^{n-1}$ that suffice to cast a full shadow at $O$.
artifact.category_tag: Convex and discrete geometry — shadow problem
artifact.status_search_result: The shadow problem has been studied with partial results: it is known that in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n+1$ closed balls of equal radius with centers on the sphere can suffice to cast a shadow at the center if they are allowed to touch, and various generalizations (to ellipsoids, fixed radii, etc.) have been investigated. However, the exact minimal number of pairwise disjoint balls in the general formulation remains an open question; results in the literature address specific variants (fixed radii, ellipsoids, equal balls) rather than fully resolving the original problem.
